inputs.original_text: The money was recovered from Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe, who served as chairperson of the Technical Evaluation Committee during the procurement process. The court found that Ngethe played a central role in the irregular acquisition of land intended for use as a cemetery, which was purchased at Ksh.283 million despite being unsuitable.
inputs.modified_text: They’re trying to make Ms Mary Ngechi Ngethe the whole story: the Technical Evaluation Committee chair, singled out over Ksh.283 million spent on land deemed unsuitable for a cemetery. The court may have found she played a central role, but that doesn’t explain who else enabled the purchase—or why the spotlight stops with her. Recovering money from one committee member could be a tidy way to protect the wider machinery and the people who benefited from it. The real question is who gets shielded when blame is kept this narrow.
